answers.good: The client sends an idempotency key header with each POST. The server stores the key together with the stored response in a table with a unique constraint; a retry with the same key returns the previous result instead of charging again. Concurrent retries race on the unique constraint inside a transaction, so only one wins.
answers.medium: I would make the endpoint idempotent by having the client pass a unique request id, and the server checks whether it has seen that id before processing the payment.
answers.poor: Payments should be fast, so I would add more servers and retry the request until it works.

answers.good: A list comprehension builds the whole list in memory immediately, while a generator expression is lazy and yields one value at a time on demand. For large or infinite streams the generator saves memory, but it is single pass: you cannot index it or reuse it after it is exhausted.
answers.medium: Generators use yield and are lazy, so they compute values when you call next on them.
answers.poor: They are basically the same thing but generators use round brackets instead of square ones.
